data.text:
The Spaniards arrived in Manila and found the settlements of the rajas along the shore near the mouth of the Pasig River, which is Tondo to this day. 

I had no idea how much land has been reclaimed from Manila Bay until I saw these old maps. Even Ermita and Malate were by the bay during these times. 

Reclamation is another cause of flooding along with the natural waterways being paved over. 

Technically, settlements shouldn't be built near the water. Look at the distance between Manila and what is now Rizal and you will see how settlements should've been built in Quezon instead of what is now Metro Manila. 

But there was no trucks to transport goods yet then so the barges going up the Pasig River were the main mode of transport. 

The culprits now are lack of urban planning and adequate flood control systems plus the indiscriminate dumping of garbage by squatters who built houses along the waterways to serve as their toilets. 

Ironically, in about another ten to twenty years, Quezon will be the only room for expansion of Metro Manila, in terms of residential-commercial space. 

The government still hasn't made any concrete plans to move the capital as Malaysia and Indonesia have done. 

It's imperative also that the national capital region be put under the authority of a governor or under the national government like Washington DC to put in order the flood control system. 

This is realistically not going to happen so we just have to hope that LGUs will be as functional as Marikina. 

While the river overflowed at 18 meters, the Wawa Dam effectively controlled water flow and the intermittent downpours also helped by allowing the river to go back to its normal level. 

Laguna, Cavite and Bulacan residents should hold their LGU officials accountable.
